10004776.p001.s001.text: Genome-Wide Analysis of MYB Transcription Factor Gene Superfamily Reveals BjPHL2a Involved in Modulating the Expression of BjCHI1 in Brassica juncea

10004776.p002.s001.text: Brassica juncea is an economically important vegetable and oilseed crop.

10004776.p002.s002.text: The MYB transcription factor superfamily is one of the largest transcription factor families in plants, and plays crucial roles in regulating the expression of key genes involved in a variety of physiological processes.

10004776.p002.s003.text: However, a systematic analysis of the MYB transcription factor genes in Brassica juncea (BjMYB) has not been performed.

10004776.p002.s004.text: In this study, a total of 502 BjMYB superfamily transcription factor genes were identified, including 23 1R-MYBs, 388 R2R3-MYBs, 16 3R-MYBs, 4 4R-MYBs, 7 atypical MYBs, and 64 MYB-CCs, which is approximately 2.4-fold larger than that of AtMYBs.

10004776.p002.s005.text: Phylogenetic relationship analysis revealed that the MYB-CC subfamily consists of 64 BjMYB-CC genes.

10004776.p002.s006.text: The expression pattern of members of PHL2 subclade homologous genes in Brassica juncea (BjPHL2) after Botrytis cinerea infection were determined, and BjPHL2a was isolated from a yeast one-hybrid screen with the promoter of BjCHI1 as bait.

10004776.p002.s007.text: BjPHL2a was found to localize mainly in the nucleus of plant cells.

10004776.p002.s008.text: An EMSA assay confirmed that BjPHL2a binds to the Wbl-4 element of BjCHI1.

10004776.p002.s009.text: Transiently expressed BjPHL2a activates expression of the GUS reporter system driven by a BjCHI1 mini-promoter in tobacco (Nicotiana benthamiana) leaves.

10004776.p002.s010.text: Taken together, our data provide a comprehensive evaluation of BjMYBs and show that BjPHL2a, one of the members of BjMYB-CCs, functions as a transcription activator by interacting with the Wbl-4 element in the promoter of BjCHI1 for targeted gene-inducible expression.

10004776.p004.s001.text: Brassica juncea is an economically important vegetable and oilseed crop widely cultivated in Asia and Europe.

10004776.p004.s002.text: In terms of the well-known “triangle of U” model, Brassica juncea is an allotetraploid (AABB, 2n = 4x = 36) improved through interspecific hybridization between the diploid progenitors Brassica rapa (AA, 2n = 20) and Brassica nigra (BB, 2n = 16), followed by spontaneous chromosome doubling.

10004776.p004.s003.text: The fungal pathogen Botrytis cinerea is a persistent threat to plants throughout the world, including Brassica juncea, causing massive yield loss in agriculture.

10004776.p004.s004.text: Chitin has been recognized as a general elicitor of plant immune responses, and is also a major structural component of the carbohydrate skeleton of the cell wall of Botrytis cinerea.

10004776.p004.s005.text: Plants have developed a sophisticated system to fight against Botrytis cinerea via catalyzing chitin cleavage in the cell wall.

10004776.p004.s006.text: Plant chitinases, a class of pathogenesis-related enzymes (PRs), play an essential role in this process via randomly cleaving internal β-1, 4 glycosidic linkages in chitin.

10004776.p005.s001.text: BjCHI1 is the first isolated chitinase gene whose expression is associated with defense against Botrytis cinerea attack in Brassica juncea.

10004776.p005.s002.text: BjCHI1 contains two chitin binding domains (CBDs), and extensive investigation has shown that inducible expression of BjCHI1 is required for defense against Botrytis cinerea.

10004776.p005.s003.text: Several cis-acting elements have been predicted in the promoter of BjCHI1 (BiC-P), and a W box-like 4 element (Wbl-4 box) was recently verified as a fungus-responsive cis-acting element.

10004776.p005.s004.text: A yeast one-hybrid (Y1H) screen with the core fungus-inducible element as bait was used to identify a number of transcription factors from a cDNA library in Brassica juncea, which were isolated and verified.

10004776.p005.s005.text: BjMYB1, an MYB-CC transcription factor, displayed binding activity to this element and activated the expression of BjCHI1.

10004776.p005.s006.text: Moreover, Bj26, a C2H2-type zinc finger protein also displayed binding and activating activity toward the Wbl-4 box.

10004776.p005.s007.text: However, the protein factors involved in the hierarchical and dynamic induction of BjCHI1 remain unclear.

10004776.p006.s001.text: The fungus-responsive Wbl-4 box in the promoter of BjCHI1 is recognized by BjMYB1, providing novel insight into the transcriptional regulation of BjCHI1.

10004776.p006.s002.text: MYB-like transcription factors are one of the largest transcription factor families in plants, they play important roles in regulating plant growth and protecting plants from various sources of stress, and they are distinguished by the presence of conserved DNA-binding domains named R repeats.

10004776.p006.s003.text: MYB transcription factors are thus classified into four subfamilies based on the number of R repeats: R2R3-MYB, 1R-MYB, 3R-MYB, and 4R-MYB.

10004776.p006.s004.text: The MYB–CC type transcription factors are a subtype within the MYB transcription factor superfamily that harbor a combination of MYB and coiled-coil (CC) motifs.

10004776.p006.s005.text: PHR1 and other MYB-CC genes modulate the phosphate starvation response in plants via binding to the PHR1-binding DNA sequence (P1BS) cis-regulatory element within either the 5’ untranslated regions (UTRs) or the promoter regions of phosphate starvation-induced (PSI) genes.

10004776.p006.s006.text: MYB and MYB-CC transcription factor genes have been well characterized in a number of plant species, such as Arabidopsis thaliana, Zea mays, rice (Oryza sativa), Brassica rapa, Brassica napus, Hedychium coronarium, Cymbidium ensifolium, Apocynum venetum, carrot (Daucus carota), mango (Mangifera indica), chili pepper, and sweet cherry (Prunus avium L.).

10004776.p006.s007.text: Nevertheless, relatively few members of the MYB transcription factors in Brassica juncea (BjMYBs) have been well explored, and there is still no comprehensive study of BjMYBs to date.

10004776.p007.s001.text: Our previous investigation revealed that BjMYB1 plays an important role in mediating the inducible expression of BjCHI1 by Botrytis cinerea and its derived elicitor chitin.

10004776.p007.s002.text: In the current study, we conducted a genome-wide exploration of the MYB transcription factor superfamily in Brassica juncea, including 23 1R-MYBs, 388 R2R3-MYBs, 16 3R-MYBs, 4 4R-MYBs, 7 atypical MYBs, and 64 MYB-CCs; phylogenetic analysis and the chromosomal location of BjMYBs were determined.

10004776.p007.s003.text: In addition, the gene structure and expression profiles of BjMYB-CCs were analyzed.

10004776.p007.s004.text: Finally, BjPHL2a was isolated and verified to be required for inducible expression of BjCHI1 via interaction with the fungus-responsive Wbl-4 box in the mini-promoter region of BjCHI1.

10004776.p010.s001.text: A total of 502 putative BjMYBs with conserved Myb-like DNA binding domains or MYB-CC domains were isolated from the genome of Brassica juncea.

10004776.p010.s002.text: This is approximatly 2.4-fold more than that of AtMYBs.

10004776.p010.s003.text: We found 241 and 230 BjMYB genes in the A and B subgenome, respectively (Table S1).

10004776.p010.s004.text: The BjMYBs were renamed in terms of their sequence similarity to AtMYBs (Table S1).

10004776.p010.s005.text: The protein lengths of BjMYBs were between 96 and 1202 amino acids (aa), with predicted molecular weights (Mw) in the range of 11.58 to 133.39 kDa.

10004776.p010.s006.text: The theoretical isoelectric points (pI) of BjMYBs ranged from 4.71 to 10.00 (Table S1).

10004776.p010.s007.text: The pI of 309 BjMYBs (60.35%) showed values greater than seven.

10004776.p010.s008.text: Other characteristics of BjMYBs, such as gene position and accession number, are presented in Table S1.

10004776.p014.s001.text: The chromosomal distribution of BjMYB genes was determined with MapChart as previously described and is illustrated in Figure 2.

10004776.p014.s002.text: The 471 identified BjMYB genes were mapped on 18 chromosomes of Brassica juncea (93.82%).

10004776.p014.s003.text: Among them, 241 BjMYB genes were mapped to the A01 to A10 chromosomes and 230 BjMYB genes were mapped to the B01 to B08 chromosomes of Brassica juncea.

10004776.p014.s004.text: In contrast, there remain 31 BjMYB genes on as yet unmapped scaffolds or contigs.

10004776.p014.s005.text: BjMYB genes were found to be scattered on each chromosome in Brassica juncea, but their distribution density differed.

10004776.p014.s006.text: Chromosomes A03 (45 members), B02 (38 members), and B03 (38 members) contained a higher density of BjMYB genes, while chromosomes A04 (12 members), A05 (16 members), and A10 (13 members) had fewer BjMYB genes anchored.

10004776.p014.s007.text: We further analyzed the chromosomal distributions of BjMYB-CC subfamily genes.

10004776.p014.s008.text: As a result, 28 BjMYB-CC subfamily genes were found on the A subgenome chromosomes and 30 on the B subgenome chromosomes.

10004776.p014.s009.text: Surprisingly, no putative BjMYB-CC genes were located on chromosome A04.

10004776.p014.s010.text: Moreover, there were six BjMYB-CC genes on as yet unmapped scaffolds or contigs.

10004776.p017.s001.text: We next constructed phylogenetic trees of AtMYB-CCs and BjMYB-CCs (Figure 4), and found that all 64 putative BjMYB-CC transcription factors were named according to their sequence similarity to the corresponding AtMYB-CC orthologues (Figure 1 and Table S1).

10004776.p017.s002.text: There were four proteins (BjuB039462, BjuA005498, BjuA012774/BjPHL2a, and BjuB032221/BjuPHL2b) categorized into the same branch as AtPHL2 in our phylogenetic tree; BjuB039462 and BjuA005498 were designated as BjPHL2b1 and BjPHL2a1, respectively.

10004776.p017.s003.text: We also observed that BjMYB1 was categorized into the same clade as BjPHL2b1 (Figure 4 and Figure S1).

10004776.p017.s004.text: Moreover, the coding sequence (CDS) of BjMYB1 displayed high sequence identity (~98%) to BjPHL2b1 (Figure S2).

10004776.p017.s005.text: Compared with BjPHL2b1, BjMYB1 was found to be missing 213-nt in the 5′ region, a 9-nt insertion in the central region, and a G to A replacement at the 3′ end, which resulted in a 71-amino acid-long deletion at the N-terminal and a YGQ insertion in the central region (Figures S1 and S3).

10004776.p017.s006.text: To further investigate the evolutionary relationships, we found a total of 10 motifs (with E-value cutoff <e-1.0), including the conserved MYB domain (motif seven), in BjMYBs (Figure S4 and Table S2).

10004776.p017.s007.text: The distribution of the conserved MYB-CC motif in each member of MYB-CCs (15 AtMYB-CCs and 64 BjMYB-CCs) was also depicted individually (Figure 4 and Table S3).

10004776.p017.s008.text: Consistent with the gene architecture, nearly all of the homologous proteins in the phylogenetic tree of the BjMYB-CC proteins displayed similar motif arrangement to their AtMYB-CC counterparts, such as the four members of BjPHL2 clade (Figure 4 and Figure S4).

10004776.p018.s001.text: 2.5. Expression Profiles of BjMYB-CC Genes in Response to Abiotic Stresses

10004776.p019.s001.text: We next investigated the transcript abundance of 64 BjMYB-CC genes in response to abiotic stresses.

10004776.p019.s002.text: The expression profiles under drought, high temperature, and salt conditions were determined using publicly available Brassica juncea RNA-seq data.

10004776.p019.s003.text: Surprisingly, only a few BjMYB-CC genes were observed to be induced in response to specific treatment (Figure 5 and Table S4).

10004776.p019.s004.text: However, many genes were observed to be repressed in response to drought or high temperature treatment.

10004776.p019.s005.text: The expression of BjMYB-CC genes under salt treatment displayed results similar to those of the control treatment (Figure 5 and Table S4).

10004776.p021.s001.text: As mentioned above, there were four BjMYB proteins categorized into the same branch as the previously identified BjMYB1 in our phylogenetic tree (Figure 4).

10004776.p021.s002.text: BjMYB1 was reported to be involved in host defense against fungal attack through activating the expression of BjCHI1 by binding to the Wbl-4 element in the promoter.

10004776.p021.s003.text: It is tempting to speculate that gene expression patterns can provide important clues for paralogous genes function.

10004776.p021.s004.text: In order to give insight into the role of BjPHL2 subclade members in plant resistance against fungal infection, we examined the expression of BjPHL2a and its paralogs after infection by Botrytis cinerea.

10004776.p021.s005.text: Quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) analysis showed that only the transcription of BjPHL2b1 was slightly induced by Botrytis cinerea, reaching a peak at 24 hours after inoculation (Figure 6).

10004776.p021.s006.text: The expression pattern of BjPHL2a1 and BjPHL2b after infection by Botrytis cinerea were similar to that of BjPHL2a (Figure 6), all of which were not significantly induced by Botrytis cinerea (no more than 1.5-fold).

10004776.p023.s001.text: We previously performed systemic Y1H screening of a cDNA library from Brassica juncea to identify putative transcriptional factors that interact with the fungus-responsive cis-acting element Wbl-4 box in the promoter of BjCHI1.

10004776.p023.s002.text: Sequencing analysis revealed that two of the isolated positive clones harbored BjcDNA (BjuA012774), which encodes a predicted protein with 297 amino acids (Figure 7A; 32.5 kDa, pI of 6.55).

10004776.p023.s003.text: The CDS of BjuA012774 was used as a query for a local BLAST (basic local alignment search tool) search in Brassica juncea CDSs downloaded from the BGD (Brassica Genomics Database).

10004776.p023.s004.text: BjuA012774 displayed high sequence identity (92%) to BjuB032221.

10004776.p023.s005.text: The protein sequences of BjuA012774 and BjuB032221 were used as a query for a BLAST search in TAIR (The Arabidopsis Information Resource).

10004776.p023.s006.text: BjuA012774 and BjuB032221 showed high sequence similarity to AtPHL2 (PHR1-LIKE2, At3g24120), which is an MYB-CC type transcription factor involved in the phosphate starvation response.

10004776.p023.s007.text: The online tool CD-Search was used to identify conserved domains in BjPHL2a.

10004776.p023.s008.text: As shown in Figure 7A, BjPHL2a contains an Myb-CC motif followed by the conserved Myb DNA-binding motif (myb_SHAQKYF).

10004776.p023.s009.text: To validate whether BjPHL2a actually possesses DNA binding and transactivation activity with the Wbl-4 box mini-promoter, we used a Y1H assay.

10004776.p023.s010.text: The full-length coding region of BjPHL2a was introduced into the vector pGADT7, which contained a GAL4 activation domain.

10004776.p023.s011.text: The resulting pGADT7-BjPHL2a plasmid was then transformed into the bait-reporter yeast strain Y1Hgold [pBait-AbAi] and mutated bait-reporter yeast strain Y1Hgold [pBait-m-AbAi], and growth of the transformants was observed.

10004776.p023.s012.text: All of the transformants grew well on SD/-Leu (no AbA) medium (Figure 7B, upper panel).

10004776.p023.s013.text: However, only yeast cells containing pGADT7-BjPHL2a grew well on the selective medium—SD/-Leu/+AbA550 (SD/-Leu media containing 550 ng/mL AbA) agar plates (Figure 7B, lower panel).

10004776.p023.s014.text: Almost no DNA binding and transactivation activity were observed in transformants where the bait-reporter yeast strains [pBait-m-AbAi] were transformed with BjPHL2a (Figure 7B, lower panel).

10004776.p023.s015.text: Taken together, these results suggest that BjPHL2a binds to the Wbl-4 box.

10004776.p024.s001.text: 2.8. BjPHL2a Encodes an MYB-CC Protein Located in the Nucleus

10004776.p025.s001.text: Sequence analysis revealed that BjPHL2a has the same motif arrangement as AtPHL2, including an MYB DNA binding motif at the N-terminus and an MYB-CC motif in the central region (Figure 7A).

10004776.p025.s002.text: However, no predicted NLS was observed in BjPHL2a, which is a typical characteristic of many transcription factors.

10004776.p025.s003.text: To understand whether BjPHL2a is a functional transcription factor, we set out to determine the subcellular localization of BjPHL2a.

10004776.p025.s004.text: The chimeric expression vector pCAMBIA1205-YFP-BjPHL2a and the control vector pCAMBIA1205-YFP were transiently expressed in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves via agroinfiltration.

10004776.p025.s005.text: We observed fluorescent signals of YFP-BjPHL2a in epidermal cells by confocal fluorescence microscopy.

10004776.p025.s006.text: As shown in Figure 8, the YFP-BjPHL2a fusion protein was found to localize predominantly in the nucleus of the cell, while YFP alone was present throughout the cell.

10004776.p025.s007.text: These data indicate that BjPHL2a is a nuclear-localized protein, consistent with most transcription factors being present in the nucleus.

10004776.p026.s002.text: BjPHL2a Binds to the Wbl-4 Element In Vitro

10004776.p027.s001.text: Previous work has demonstrated that the MYB-core element [C/T]NGTT[G/A], AC-elements (ACC[A/T]A[A/C][T/C] and ACC[A/T][A/C/T][A/C/T]), and cis-regulatory elements are recognized by R2R3-type MYB transcription factors.

10004776.p027.s002.text: The MYB-CC protein BjMYB1 binds to W-box or W-box-like elements, but not to AC elements.

10004776.p027.s003.text: To determine whether nuclear-localized BjPHL2a actually possesses DNA binding activity, we used an electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA).

10004776.p027.s004.text: His-tagged BjPHL2a recombinant protein was purified and used for EMSA.

10004776.p027.s005.text: A shifted band was observed when His-BjPHL2a was incubated with a labeled Wbl-4 box (hot probe, Figure 9A, W4).

10004776.p027.s006.text: This shift could be competed out with a huge amount (50× or 200×) of non-labeled Wbl-4 element (cold probe, Figure 9A, W4), indicating that BjPHL2a is capable of binding to the Wbl-4 element.

10004776.p027.s007.text: Furthermore, when the Wbl-5 box was used, almost no shifted band was observed (Figure 9B, W5).

10004776.p027.s008.text: In contrast, when the TGAC core sequence of Wbl-4 element was removed, the shifted band was not observed, indicating that deletion of the core sequence TGAC abolished the binding of BjPHL2a to the Wbl-4 element (Figure 9A, W4D).

10004776.p027.s009.text: These results indicate that recombinant BjPHL2a proteins could interact with the Wbl-4 element.

10004776.p028.s002.text: BjPHL2a Activates a Mini-Promoter Containing a Wbl-4 Element In Vivo

10004776.p029.s001.text: To further analyze whether BjPHL2a actually had transactivation activity in vivo, we sought to directly investigate its role in transactivating the Wbl-4 element by transient expression in Nicotiana benthamiana.

10004776.p029.s002.text: As previously described, we also recruited several key deletion derivatives of the BjCHI1 promoter, such as P9, P16, P53, P27, and P45 (Figure 9A) as promoters for GUS fusion reporter plasmids.

10004776.p029.s003.text: Consistent with previous reports, BjPHL2a activated the expression of GUS driven by P16-, P27-, and P45 promoters containing Wbl-4 box, but not by P53 and P9 (Figure 10B,C).

10004776.p029.s004.text: Compared with P16, only the TGAC in the core sequence of the Wbl-4 element was absent in P53 and the Wbl-4 box was removed in P9.

10004776.p029.s005.text: Therefore, these observations indicate that BjPHL2a can also transactivate the Wbl-4 element in vivo.

10004776.p031.s001.text: The MYB-like superfamily transcription factors are one of the largest transcription factor families in plants and play important roles in a wide range of physiological processes, such as light signaling, the anthocyanin biosynthetic pathway, hypocotyl elongation, phosphate starvation, and resistance to biotic and abiotic stresses.

10004776.p031.s002.text: Although MYB and MYB-CC transcription factor genes have been identified in a number of plant species at the genome-wide level, there is little information available on this superfamily in the Brassica juncea genome.

10004776.p031.s003.text: Recently, bioinformatics and publicly released data sets describing the genome and transcriptome of Brassica juncea have paved the way for systemically exploring this important crop species.

10004776.p031.s004.text: In the present study, a total of 502 BjMYB genes were identified in Brassica juncea, which were divided into six subfamilies (1R-, R2R3-, 3R-, 4R-, atypical MYBs, and MYB-CCs) and clustered into 15 groups (Figure 1 and Table S1).

10004776.p031.s005.text: The number of BjMYB genes was greater than those of Arabidopsis thaliana (212), Oryza sativa (213), Zea mays (169), Brassica rapa (354), and Brassica oleracea (330), but fewer than that in Brassica napus (556).

10004776.p031.s006.text: BjMYB proteins were not equally distributed into 15 different groups in the phylogenetic tree (Figure 1).

10004776.p031.s007.text: Among them, the top largest groups (C1, C9, C13, C14, and C15) represented around 70% of the total BjMYB members (Figure 1 and Table S1), suggesting that these groups may be highly differentiated in the Brassica juncea genome.

10004776.p031.s008.text: Moreover, the large range of Mw and pI of BjMYBs suggests their functional diversity in distinct biological processes, which may be attributed to their difference in full-length amino acid sequences and rest domains, in addition to similarity in MYB domains.

10004776.p032.s001.text: As displayed in Figure 2, the 471 (93.82%) identified members of BjMYB genes were unevenly distributed across all 18 chromosomes at different densities.

10004776.p032.s002.text: Among them, 241 BjMYB genes were mapped to the A subgenome and 230 BjMYB genes to the B subgenome of Brassica juncea.

10004776.p032.s003.text: The chromosomes A01 to A10 and B01 to B08 represent the two parental diploid ancestors of Brassica juncea.

10004776.p032.s004.text: The number of BjMYB genes (502) was found to be less than the sum of its two parental lines, Brassica rapa (301) and Brassica nigra (>300), indicating loss of MYB genes also happened after allopolyplodization.

10004776.p032.s005.text: In general, every AtMYB-CC was expected to have four to six homologs in Brassica juncea.

10004776.p032.s006.text: Consistently, 15 AtMYB-CCs had 64 homologous genes in Brassica juncea (Figure 4A and Table S1).

10004776.p032.s007.text: For example, AtPHL2 had four homologs (BjPHL2a, BjPHL2b, BjPHL2a1, and BjPHL2b1) and AtPHR1 had five homologs (BjPHR1a, BjPHR1b, BjPHR1a1, BjPHR1b1, and BjPHR1b2).

10004776.p032.s008.text: In terms of the overall gene structure, significant differences were found in the number of introns among BjMYB-CC subfamily members (Figure 3).

10004776.p032.s009.text: However, the overall intron/exon distribution within members of the same subclade was highly similar, such as PHL2-, PHL3-, and PHR1-subclade (Figure 3), indicating that the biological significance of these homologous genes may be redundantly conserved to a certain extent.

10004776.p033.s001.text: It is tempting to speculate that gene expression patterns can provide important clues for gene function.

10004776.p033.s002.text: The expression patterns of 64 BjMYB-CC genes from three type of abiotic stresses were determined (Figure 5).

10004776.p033.s003.text: Only a few BjMYB-CC genes displayed inducible expression by at least one analyzed treatment (Figure 5 and Table S4).

10004776.p033.s004.text: Furthermore, qRT-PCR analysis revealed similar expression patterns after Botrytis cinerea infection of the three AtPHL2 homologs in Brassica juncea (BjPHL2a, BjPHL2b, and BjPHL2a1, Figure 6).

10004776.p034.s001.text: Previous work has shown that the MYB-CC transcription factor BjMYB1 can bind to W-box or W-box-like elements, but not to AC elements.

10004776.p034.s002.text: As mentioned above, MYB–CC type transcription factors are a distinct subfamily of the plant MYB superfamily, which were originally identified as phosphate starvation response (PHR) protein family transcription factors, such as AtPHR1 and OsPHR2.

10004776.p034.s003.text: It is well known that PHR protein family members can transactivate the expression of a broad range of PSI genes by binding to P1BS cis-elements in a phosphate (Pi)-dependent manner.

10004776.p034.s004.text: The P1BS cis-regulatory element is characterized by the nucleotide motif GNATATNC or CATATATG.

10004776.p034.s005.text: We also observed a putative P1BS-like cis-element (CATATATCG) near the fungus-responsive Wbl-4 box in the promoter of BjCHI1.

10004776.p034.s006.text: Besides serving as master transcriptional regulators of the phosphate sensing pathway, PHR1-like MYB-CC proteins (such as AtPHR1 and OsPHR1/2/3) have been recently reported to play central roles in the balance between nutrient stress response and immune regulation or mycorrhizal symbiosis with respect to root microbiota.

10004776.p034.s007.text: One possibility is that the observed binding activity of MYB-CC-like proteins (BjMYB1 and BjPHL2a) to the Wbl-4 box containing mini-promoter may also be partially attributed to the putative P1BS-like cis-element near the Wbl-4 box.

10004776.p034.s008.text: In other words, PHR1-like MYB-CC proteins may also have roles in fighting against Botrytis cinerea infection via modulating the expression of BjCHI1.

10004776.p034.s009.text: We found four AtPHL2 homologs in Brassica juncea and similar expression patterns after Botrytis cinerea infection was observed among three paralogs (Figure 6).

10004776.p034.s010.text: The previously isolated BjMYB1 showed sequence differences compared with other BjPHL2 s (Figures S1–S3).

10004776.p034.s011.text: Therefore, it is possible that BjPHL2a, together with the closed paralogs, may be redundantly involved in fighting against fungal attack by interacting with the Wbl-4 element in the promoter of BjCHI1.

10004776.p035.s001.text: Recently, hierarchical and dynamic regulation of defense-responsive genes by AtMYB51 and AtWRKY33 has been reported.

10004776.p035.s002.text: The cognate nucleotide motif of the Wbl-4 box (GTGACT), also shows a minor difference to the core nucleotide sequence of classical W-boxes (C/TTGACC/T).

10004776.p035.s003.text: This may be the major reason that we have not isolated any WRKY-like transcription factors to date.

10004776.p035.s004.text: However, another possibility is that BjPHL2a or BjMYB1 and BjWRKY transcription factors may function coordinately to control the inducible expression of BjCHI1.

10004776.p061.s001.text: In the present study, the identification, classification, and expression analysis of the MYB gene superfamily was comprehensively evaluated at the whole genome level in Brassica juncea.

10004776.p061.s002.text: Functional and molecular studies showed that BjPHL2a functions as a transcription activator by interacting with the Wbl-4 element in the promoter of BjCHI1 for targeted gene inducible expression after Botrytis cinerea infection.

PMC10004776.p001.text: Genome-Wide Analysis of MYB Transcription Factor Gene Superfamily Reveals BjPHL2a Involved in Modulating the Expression of BjCHI1 in Brassica juncea

PMC10004776.p002.text: Brassica juncea is an economically important vegetable and oilseed crop. The MYB transcription factor superfamily is one of the largest transcription factor families in plants, and plays crucial roles in regulating the expression of key genes involved in a variety of physiological processes. However, a systematic analysis of the MYB transcription factor genes in Brassica juncea (BjMYB) has not been performed. In this study, a total of 502 BjMYB superfamily transcription factor genes were identified, including 23 1R-MYBs, 388 R2R3-MYBs, 16 3R-MYBs, 4 4R-MYBs, 7 atypical MYBs, and 64 MYB-CCs, which is approximately 2.4-fold larger than that of AtMYBs. Phylogenetic relationship analysis revealed that the MYB-CC subfamily consists of 64 BjMYB-CC genes. The expression pattern of members of PHL2 subclade homologous genes in Brassica juncea (BjPHL2) after Botrytis cinerea infection were determined, and BjPHL2a was isolated from a yeast one-hybrid screen with the promoter of BjCHI1 as bait. BjPHL2a was found to localize mainly in the nucleus of plant cells. An EMSA assay confirmed that BjPHL2a binds to the Wbl-4 element of BjCHI1. Transiently expressed BjPHL2a activates expression of the GUS reporter system driven by a BjCHI1 mini-promoter in tobacco (Nicotiana benthamiana) leaves. Taken together, our data provide a comprehensive evaluation of BjMYBs and show that BjPHL2a, one of the members of BjMYB-CCs, functions as a transcription activator by interacting with the Wbl-4 element in the promoter of BjCHI1 for targeted gene-inducible expression.

PMC10004776.p004.text: Brassica juncea is an economically important vegetable and oilseed crop widely cultivated in Asia and Europe. In terms of the well-known “triangle of U” model, Brassica juncea is an allotetraploid (AABB, 2n = 4x = 36) improved through interspecific hybridization between the diploid progenitors Brassica rapa (AA, 2n = 20) and Brassica nigra (BB, 2n = 16), followed by spontaneous chromosome doubling. The fungal pathogen Botrytis cinerea is a persistent threat to plants throughout the world, including Brassica juncea, causing massive yield loss in agriculture. Chitin has been recognized as a general elicitor of plant immune responses, and is also a major structural component of the carbohydrate skeleton of the cell wall of Botrytis cinerea. Plants have developed a sophisticated system to fight against Botrytis cinerea via catalyzing chitin cleavage in the cell wall. Plant chitinases, a class of pathogenesis-related enzymes (PRs), play an essential role in this process via randomly cleaving internal β-1, 4 glycosidic linkages in chitin.

PMC10004776.p005.text: BjCHI1 is the first isolated chitinase gene whose expression is associated with defense against Botrytis cinerea attack in Brassica juncea. BjCHI1 contains two chitin binding domains (CBDs), and extensive investigation has shown that inducible expression of BjCHI1 is required for defense against Botrytis cinerea. Several cis-acting elements have been predicted in the promoter of BjCHI1 (BiC-P), and a W box-like 4 element (Wbl-4 box) was recently verified as a fungus-responsive cis-acting element. A yeast one-hybrid (Y1H) screen with the core fungus-inducible element as bait was used to identify a number of transcription factors from a cDNA library in Brassica juncea, which were isolated and verified. BjMYB1, an MYB-CC transcription factor, displayed binding activity to this element and activated the expression of BjCHI1. Moreover, Bj26, a C2H2-type zinc finger protein also displayed binding and activating activity toward the Wbl-4 box. However, the protein factors involved in the hierarchical and dynamic induction of BjCHI1 remain unclear.

PMC10004776.p006.text: The fungus-responsive Wbl-4 box in the promoter of BjCHI1 is recognized by BjMYB1, providing novel insight into the transcriptional regulation of BjCHI1. MYB-like transcription factors are one of the largest transcription factor families in plants, they play important roles in regulating plant growth and protecting plants from various sources of stress, and they are distinguished by the presence of conserved DNA-binding domains named R repeats. MYB transcription factors are thus classified into four subfamilies based on the number of R repeats: R2R3-MYB, 1R-MYB, 3R-MYB, and 4R-MYB. The MYB–CC type transcription factors are a subtype within the MYB transcription factor superfamily that harbor a combination of MYB and coiled-coil (CC) motifs. PHR1 and other MYB-CC genes modulate the phosphate starvation response in plants via binding to the PHR1-binding DNA sequence (P1BS) cis-regulatory element within either the 5’ untranslated regions (UTRs) or the promoter regions of phosphate starvation-induced (PSI) genes. MYB and MYB-CC transcription factor genes have been well characterized in a number of plant species, such as Arabidopsis thaliana, Zea mays, rice (Oryza sativa), Brassica rapa, Brassica napus, Hedychium coronarium, Cymbidium ensifolium, Apocynum venetum, carrot (Daucus carota), mango (Mangifera indica), chili pepper, and sweet cherry (Prunus avium L.). Nevertheless, relatively few members of the MYB transcription factors in Brassica juncea (BjMYBs) have been well explored, and there is still no comprehensive study of BjMYBs to date.

PMC10004776.p007.text: Our previous investigation revealed that BjMYB1 plays an important role in mediating the inducible expression of BjCHI1 by Botrytis cinerea and its derived elicitor chitin. In the current study, we conducted a genome-wide exploration of the MYB transcription factor superfamily in Brassica juncea, including 23 1R-MYBs, 388 R2R3-MYBs, 16 3R-MYBs, 4 4R-MYBs, 7 atypical MYBs, and 64 MYB-CCs; phylogenetic analysis and the chromosomal location of BjMYBs were determined. In addition, the gene structure and expression profiles of BjMYB-CCs were analyzed. Finally, BjPHL2a was isolated and verified to be required for inducible expression of BjCHI1 via interaction with the fungus-responsive Wbl-4 box in the mini-promoter region of BjCHI1.

PMC10004776.p010.text: A total of 502 putative BjMYBs with conserved Myb-like DNA binding domains or MYB-CC domains were isolated from the genome of Brassica juncea. This is approximatly 2.4-fold more than that of AtMYBs. We found 241 and 230 BjMYB genes in the A and B subgenome, respectively (Table S1). The BjMYBs were renamed in terms of their sequence similarity to AtMYBs (Table S1). The protein lengths of BjMYBs were between 96 and 1202 amino acids (aa), with predicted molecular weights (Mw) in the range of 11.58 to 133.39 kDa. The theoretical isoelectric points (pI) of BjMYBs ranged from 4.71 to 10.00 (Table S1). The pI of 309 BjMYBs (60.35%) showed values greater than seven. Other characteristics of BjMYBs, such as gene position and accession number, are presented in Table S1.

PMC10004776.p014.text: The chromosomal distribution of BjMYB genes was determined with MapChart as previously described and is illustrated in Figure 2. The 471 identified BjMYB genes were mapped on 18 chromosomes of Brassica juncea (93.82%). Among them, 241 BjMYB genes were mapped to the A01 to A10 chromosomes and 230 BjMYB genes were mapped to the B01 to B08 chromosomes of Brassica juncea. In contrast, there remain 31 BjMYB genes on as yet unmapped scaffolds or contigs. BjMYB genes were found to be scattered on each chromosome in Brassica juncea, but their distribution density differed. Chromosomes A03 (45 members), B02 (38 members), and B03 (38 members) contained a higher density of BjMYB genes, while chromosomes A04 (12 members), A05 (16 members), and A10 (13 members) had fewer BjMYB genes anchored. We further analyzed the chromosomal distributions of BjMYB-CC subfamily genes. As a result, 28 BjMYB-CC subfamily genes were found on the A subgenome chromosomes and 30 on the B subgenome chromosomes. Surprisingly, no putative BjMYB-CC genes were located on chromosome A04. Moreover, there were six BjMYB-CC genes on as yet unmapped scaffolds or contigs.

PMC10004776.p017.text: We next constructed phylogenetic trees of AtMYB-CCs and BjMYB-CCs (Figure 4), and found that all 64 putative BjMYB-CC transcription factors were named according to their sequence similarity to the corresponding AtMYB-CC orthologues (Figure 1 and Table S1). There were four proteins (BjuB039462, BjuA005498, BjuA012774/BjPHL2a, and BjuB032221/BjuPHL2b) categorized into the same branch as AtPHL2 in our phylogenetic tree; BjuB039462 and BjuA005498 were designated as BjPHL2b1 and BjPHL2a1, respectively. We also observed that BjMYB1 was categorized into the same clade as BjPHL2b1 (Figure 4 and Figure S1). Moreover, the coding sequence (CDS) of BjMYB1 displayed high sequence identity (~98%) to BjPHL2b1 (Figure S2). Compared with BjPHL2b1, BjMYB1 was found to be missing 213-nt in the 5′ region, a 9-nt insertion in the central region, and a G to A replacement at the 3′ end, which resulted in a 71-amino acid-long deletion at the N-terminal and a YGQ insertion in the central region (Figures S1 and S3). To further investigate the evolutionary relationships, we found a total of 10 motifs (with E-value cutoff <e-1.0), including the conserved MYB domain (motif seven), in BjMYBs (Figure S4 and Table S2). The distribution of the conserved MYB-CC motif in each member of MYB-CCs (15 AtMYB-CCs and 64 BjMYB-CCs) was also depicted individually (Figure 4 and Table S3). Consistent with the gene architecture, nearly all of the homologous proteins in the phylogenetic tree of the BjMYB-CC proteins displayed similar motif arrangement to their AtMYB-CC counterparts, such as the four members of BjPHL2 clade (Figure 4 and Figure S4).

PMC10004776.p018.text: 2.5. Expression Profiles of BjMYB-CC Genes in Response to Abiotic Stresses

PMC10004776.p019.text: We next investigated the transcript abundance of 64 BjMYB-CC genes in response to abiotic stresses. The expression profiles under drought, high temperature, and salt conditions were determined using publicly available Brassica juncea RNA-seq data. Surprisingly, only a few BjMYB-CC genes were observed to be induced in response to specific treatment (Figure 5 and Table S4). However, many genes were observed to be repressed in response to drought or high temperature treatment. The expression of BjMYB-CC genes under salt treatment displayed results similar to those of the control treatment (Figure 5 and Table S4).

PMC10004776.p021.text: As mentioned above, there were four BjMYB proteins categorized into the same branch as the previously identified BjMYB1 in our phylogenetic tree (Figure 4). BjMYB1 was reported to be involved in host defense against fungal attack through activating the expression of BjCHI1 by binding to the Wbl-4 element in the promoter. It is tempting to speculate that gene expression patterns can provide important clues for paralogous genes function. In order to give insight into the role of BjPHL2 subclade members in plant resistance against fungal infection, we examined the expression of BjPHL2a and its paralogs after infection by Botrytis cinerea. Quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) analysis showed that only the transcription of BjPHL2b1 was slightly induced by Botrytis cinerea, reaching a peak at 24 hours after inoculation (Figure 6). The expression pattern of BjPHL2a1 and BjPHL2b after infection by Botrytis cinerea were similar to that of BjPHL2a (Figure 6), all of which were not significantly induced by Botrytis cinerea (no more than 1.5-fold).

PMC10004776.p023.text: We previously performed systemic Y1H screening of a cDNA library from Brassica juncea to identify putative transcriptional factors that interact with the fungus-responsive cis-acting element Wbl-4 box in the promoter of BjCHI1. Sequencing analysis revealed that two of the isolated positive clones harbored BjcDNA (BjuA012774), which encodes a predicted protein with 297 amino acids (Figure 7A; 32.5 kDa, pI of 6.55). The CDS of BjuA012774 was used as a query for a local BLAST (basic local alignment search tool) search in Brassica juncea CDSs downloaded from the BGD (Brassica Genomics Database). BjuA012774 displayed high sequence identity (92%) to BjuB032221. The protein sequences of BjuA012774 and BjuB032221 were used as a query for a BLAST search in TAIR (The Arabidopsis Information Resource). BjuA012774 and BjuB032221 showed high sequence similarity to AtPHL2 (PHR1-LIKE2, At3g24120), which is an MYB-CC type transcription factor involved in the phosphate starvation response. The online tool CD-Search was used to identify conserved domains in BjPHL2a. As shown in Figure 7A, BjPHL2a contains an Myb-CC motif followed by the conserved Myb DNA-binding motif (myb_SHAQKYF). To validate whether BjPHL2a actually possesses DNA binding and transactivation activity with the Wbl-4 box mini-promoter, we used a Y1H assay. The full-length coding region of BjPHL2a was introduced into the vector pGADT7, which contained a GAL4 activation domain. The resulting pGADT7-BjPHL2a plasmid was then transformed into the bait-reporter yeast strain Y1Hgold [pBait-AbAi] and mutated bait-reporter yeast strain Y1Hgold [pBait-m-AbAi], and growth of the transformants was observed. All of the transformants grew well on SD/-Leu (no AbA) medium (Figure 7B, upper panel). However, only yeast cells containing pGADT7-BjPHL2a grew well on the selective medium—SD/-Leu/+AbA550 (SD/-Leu media containing 550 ng/mL AbA) agar plates (Figure 7B, lower panel). Almost no DNA binding and transactivation activity were observed in transformants where the bait-reporter yeast strains [pBait-m-AbAi] were transformed with BjPHL2a (Figure 7B, lower panel). Taken together, these results suggest that BjPHL2a binds to the Wbl-4 box.

PMC10004776.p024.text: 2.8. BjPHL2a Encodes an MYB-CC Protein Located in the Nucleus

PMC10004776.p025.text: Sequence analysis revealed that BjPHL2a has the same motif arrangement as AtPHL2, including an MYB DNA binding motif at the N-terminus and an MYB-CC motif in the central region (Figure 7A). However, no predicted NLS was observed in BjPHL2a, which is a typical characteristic of many transcription factors. To understand whether BjPHL2a is a functional transcription factor, we set out to determine the subcellular localization of BjPHL2a. The chimeric expression vector pCAMBIA1205-YFP-BjPHL2a and the control vector pCAMBIA1205-YFP were transiently expressed in Nicotiana benthamiana leaves via agroinfiltration. We observed fluorescent signals of YFP-BjPHL2a in epidermal cells by confocal fluorescence microscopy. As shown in Figure 8, the YFP-BjPHL2a fusion protein was found to localize predominantly in the nucleus of the cell, while YFP alone was present throughout the cell. These data indicate that BjPHL2a is a nuclear-localized protein, consistent with most transcription factors being present in the nucleus.

PMC10004776.p026.text: 2.9. BjPHL2a Binds to the Wbl-4 Element In Vitro

PMC10004776.p027.text: Previous work has demonstrated that the MYB-core element [C/T]NGTT[G/A], AC-elements (ACC[A/T]A[A/C][T/C] and ACC[A/T][A/C/T][A/C/T]), and cis-regulatory elements are recognized by R2R3-type MYB transcription factors. The MYB-CC protein BjMYB1 binds to W-box or W-box-like elements, but not to AC elements. To determine whether nuclear-localized BjPHL2a actually possesses DNA binding activity, we used an electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA). His-tagged BjPHL2a recombinant protein was purified and used for EMSA. A shifted band was observed when His-BjPHL2a was incubated with a labeled Wbl-4 box (hot probe, Figure 9A, W4). This shift could be competed out with a huge amount (50× or 200×) of non-labeled Wbl-4 element (cold probe, Figure 9A, W4), indicating that BjPHL2a is capable of binding to the Wbl-4 element. Furthermore, when the Wbl-5 box was used, almost no shifted band was observed (Figure 9B, W5). In contrast, when the TGAC core sequence of Wbl-4 element was removed, the shifted band was not observed, indicating that deletion of the core sequence TGAC abolished the binding of BjPHL2a to the Wbl-4 element (Figure 9A, W4D). These results indicate that recombinant BjPHL2a proteins could interact with the Wbl-4 element.

PMC10004776.p028.text: 2.10. BjPHL2a Activates a Mini-Promoter Containing a Wbl-4 Element In Vivo

PMC10004776.p029.text: To further analyze whether BjPHL2a actually had transactivation activity in vivo, we sought to directly investigate its role in transactivating the Wbl-4 element by transient expression in Nicotiana benthamiana. As previously described, we also recruited several key deletion derivatives of the BjCHI1 promoter, such as P9, P16, P53, P27, and P45 (Figure 9A) as promoters for GUS fusion reporter plasmids. Consistent with previous reports, BjPHL2a activated the expression of GUS driven by P16-, P27-, and P45 promoters containing Wbl-4 box, but not by P53 and P9 (Figure 10B,C). Compared with P16, only the TGAC in the core sequence of the Wbl-4 element was absent in P53 and the Wbl-4 box was removed in P9. Therefore, these observations indicate that BjPHL2a can also transactivate the Wbl-4 element in vivo.

PMC10004776.p031.text: The MYB-like superfamily transcription factors are one of the largest transcription factor families in plants and play important roles in a wide range of physiological processes, such as light signaling, the anthocyanin biosynthetic pathway, hypocotyl elongation, phosphate starvation, and resistance to biotic and abiotic stresses. Although MYB and MYB-CC transcription factor genes have been identified in a number of plant species at the genome-wide level, there is little information available on this superfamily in the Brassica juncea genome. Recently, bioinformatics and publicly released data sets describing the genome and transcriptome of Brassica juncea have paved the way for systemically exploring this important crop species. In the present study, a total of 502 BjMYB genes were identified in Brassica juncea, which were divided into six subfamilies (1R-, R2R3-, 3R-, 4R-, atypical MYBs, and MYB-CCs) and clustered into 15 groups (Figure 1 and Table S1). The number of BjMYB genes was greater than those of Arabidopsis thaliana (212), Oryza sativa (213), Zea mays (169), Brassica rapa (354), and Brassica oleracea (330), but fewer than that in Brassica napus (556). BjMYB proteins were not equally distributed into 15 different groups in the phylogenetic tree (Figure 1). Among them, the top largest groups (C1, C9, C13, C14, and C15) represented around 70% of the total BjMYB members (Figure 1 and Table S1), suggesting that these groups may be highly differentiated in the Brassica juncea genome. Moreover, the large range of Mw and pI of BjMYBs suggests their functional diversity in distinct biological processes, which may be attributed to their difference in full-length amino acid sequences and rest domains, in addition to similarity in MYB domains.

PMC10004776.p032.text: As displayed in Figure 2, the 471 (93.82%) identified members of BjMYB genes were unevenly distributed across all 18 chromosomes at different densities. Among them, 241 BjMYB genes were mapped to the A subgenome and 230 BjMYB genes to the B subgenome of Brassica juncea. The chromosomes A01 to A10 and B01 to B08 represent the two parental diploid ancestors of Brassica juncea. The number of BjMYB genes (502) was found to be less than the sum of its two parental lines, Brassica rapa (301) and Brassica nigra (>300), indicating loss of MYB genes also happened after allopolyplodization. In general, every AtMYB-CC was expected to have four to six homologs in Brassica juncea. Consistently, 15 AtMYB-CCs had 64 homologous genes in Brassica juncea (Figure 4A and Table S1). For example, AtPHL2 had four homologs (BjPHL2a, BjPHL2b, BjPHL2a1, and BjPHL2b1) and AtPHR1 had five homologs (BjPHR1a, BjPHR1b, BjPHR1a1, BjPHR1b1, and BjPHR1b2). In terms of the overall gene structure, significant differences were found in the number of introns among BjMYB-CC subfamily members (Figure 3). However, the overall intron/exon distribution within members of the same subclade was highly similar, such as PHL2-, PHL3-, and PHR1-subclade (Figure 3), indicating that the biological significance of these homologous genes may be redundantly conserved to a certain extent.

PMC10004776.p033.text: It is tempting to speculate that gene expression patterns can provide important clues for gene function. The expression patterns of 64 BjMYB-CC genes from three type of abiotic stresses were determined (Figure 5). Only a few BjMYB-CC genes displayed inducible expression by at least one analyzed treatment (Figure 5 and Table S4). Furthermore, qRT-PCR analysis revealed similar expression patterns after Botrytis cinerea infection of the three AtPHL2 homologs in Brassica juncea (BjPHL2a, BjPHL2b, and BjPHL2a1, Figure 6).

PMC10004776.p034.text: Previous work has shown that the MYB-CC transcription factor BjMYB1 can bind to W-box or W-box-like elements, but not to AC elements. As mentioned above, MYB–CC type transcription factors are a distinct subfamily of the plant MYB superfamily, which were originally identified as phosphate starvation response (PHR) protein family transcription factors, such as AtPHR1 and OsPHR2. It is well known that PHR protein family members can transactivate the expression of a broad range of PSI genes by binding to P1BS cis-elements in a phosphate (Pi)-dependent manner. The P1BS cis-regulatory element is characterized by the nucleotide motif GNATATNC or CATATATG. We also observed a putative P1BS-like cis-element (CATATATCG) near the fungus-responsive Wbl-4 box in the promoter of BjCHI1. Besides serving as master transcriptional regulators of the phosphate sensing pathway, PHR1-like MYB-CC proteins (such as AtPHR1 and OsPHR1/2/3) have been recently reported to play central roles in the balance between nutrient stress response and immune regulation or mycorrhizal symbiosis with respect to root microbiota. One possibility is that the observed binding activity of MYB-CC-like proteins (BjMYB1 and BjPHL2a) to the Wbl-4 box containing mini-promoter may also be partially attributed to the putative P1BS-like cis-element near the Wbl-4 box. In other words, PHR1-like MYB-CC proteins may also have roles in fighting against Botrytis cinerea infection via modulating the expression of BjCHI1. We found four AtPHL2 homologs in Brassica juncea and similar expression patterns after Botrytis cinerea infection was observed among three paralogs (Figure 6). The previously isolated BjMYB1 showed sequence differences compared with other BjPHL2 s (Figures S1–S3). Therefore, it is possible that BjPHL2a, together with the closed paralogs, may be redundantly involved in fighting against fungal attack by interacting with the Wbl-4 element in the promoter of BjCHI1.

PMC10004776.p035.text: Recently, hierarchical and dynamic regulation of defense-responsive genes by AtMYB51 and AtWRKY33 has been reported. The cognate nucleotide motif of the Wbl-4 box (GTGACT), also shows a minor difference to the core nucleotide sequence of classical W-boxes (C/TTGACC/T). This may be the major reason that we have not isolated any WRKY-like transcription factors to date. However, another possibility is that BjPHL2a or BjMYB1 and BjWRKY transcription factors may function coordinately to control the inducible expression of BjCHI1.

PMC10004776.p061.text: In the present study, the identification, classification, and expression analysis of the MYB gene superfamily was comprehensively evaluated at the whole genome level in Brassica juncea. Functional and molecular studies showed that BjPHL2a functions as a transcription activator by interacting with the Wbl-4 element in the promoter of BjCHI1 for targeted gene inducible expression after Botrytis cinerea infection.
